your own AI to Yaxxa, accessibility for callers who need it, Mitel and Avaya office phones, ad cost tiles, safer Google sign-in, and limits and billing for installations.

Connect your own AI: Claude, ChatGPT and other AI tools that speak MCP can sign in to Yaxxa and read your centre's data: customers, tickets, call timelines and transcripts, the live floor, QA, campaigns, leads, reports and the audit log, 37 read tools in all. Each person approves the connection on a consent page, sees only what they may already see, and can disconnect it under My connected AI tools. Customer details are always masked, every call is logged, and an admin can switch single tools off. It is off until your plan includes it and an admin switches it on.

Accessibility: a record of a customer's accessibility needs, saved only with their consent and seen only by people with the new accessibility permission; agents see a neutral note on what to do, never the need itself. A queue step can let a caller press a key to continue by SMS or WhatsApp and keep their place in the queue, offer flagged callers first to agents with an accessibility skill, and send a caller a live caption link that shows the conversation as it is spoken. It is off until a platform operator or reseller switches it on for your tenant.

Mitel and Avaya office phones: MiVoice Business, MX-ONE, MiVoice Office 400, IP Office and Aura connect as SIP trunks, with a setup guide for each model. TLS trunks use port 5061 by default. Extension presence is not read from these phones yet.

Ad cost tiles: dashboards can show ad spend, leads and sales from ads, and the cost per lead and per sale by day, in your organisation's currency. The tiles need the Sales feature and show only to people who see all deals.

Google sign-in: an email address that already has an account is joined to Google only after that account's password and two-step code are given, never on Google's word alone.

Install entitlements: a platform operator sets what each installation may use (modules, the reseller and billing areas, and limits on organisations, agent seats, calls at the same time and AI minutes a month), and the installation keeps to it from its next licence renewal. Nothing is ever deleted: a module that is left out is switched off with its data kept, incoming calls are never refused, and operators are told as limits come near. An installation can be billed to a reseller: its packages and modules go on that reseller's bill at the reseller's own prices, shared by day when they change part-way through the cycle. An installation that may use everything has no limits and no bill lines."}
